subject: red giant star
title: A Star Spent 7 Years Spiraling Inside a Giant 350 Times the Sun

scenes.text: A star spent seven years falling inside another star.
The giant, in the Andromeda galaxy, was 350 times wider than our Sun.
Its smaller partner orbited so close it ended up inside the giant's outer layers.
Every lap through that gas braked it, and it spiraled in for about seven orbits.
In October 2025 it appears to have hit the core. Scientists compared it to a bomb going off inside a living star.
Most mergers like this take thousands of orbits. This one took seven, and we caught it happening.

description:
A star smaller than the Sun spent about seven years spiraling inside a giant star 350 times wider than the Sun, then erupted.
The pair, nicknamed Bao (AT 2025abao), sits in the Andromeda galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away. The giant had about 7 times the Sun's mass and its companion about 0.7. The giant began brightening around 2018, erupted in October 2025, and NASA's Webb telescope observed it 47 days after the peak. The team (Karambelkar et al., Nature, 18 November 2026) says the companion was dragged in over about seven orbits, while comparable mergers take thousands; follow-up observations are still needed to confirm the stars fully merged.
What should we cover next from deep space?
first_comment: The giant was 350 times wider than the Sun. Its partner fell all the way to the core in seven orbits. Would you have bet on the little one?
